paper_metadata.title: Predicting creep-fatigue and thermomechanical fatigue life of Ni-base superalloys using a physics-guided neural network
paper_metadata.journal: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures

evidence.quote: provides a comprehensive picture of the performance of existing SX and DS superalloys
possibly other secondary microstructural influences such as the γ0 precipitate volume fraction and morphology were not included in the present work

conditions.test_method: 20%/80% random test/train split, averaged over 10 trainings

evidence.quote: the model was trained 10 times using a randomly selected 20%/80% test train split each time and then evaluated with MSE each time with an average result of 0.188 ± 0.041

conditions.test_method: all data training, averaged over 10 predictions

evidence.quote: The average MSE of 10 predictions from the model trained with all data is 0.168 ± 0.011.

The model was evaluated with five-fold cross validation using the metric MSE from Equation 12 to score the accuracy of model for each tested fold that resulted in an average cross validation score of 0.186 ± 0.025.

compressive dwells continue to be detrimental at low strain ranges, resulting in a steeper strain-life curve, which likely related to an oxidation-fatigue interaction consistent with what has been observed experimentally.
